trigger: The Phase-A curated 1901-1950 comparison reached AUROC 0.921 while the separately defined native-generator 1901-1950 auxiliary comparison reached AUROC 0.536. This raises a generator-domain alternative that the frozen primary comparison alone cannot exclude.
selection_rule: Use all nine, and only the nine, independent pre-1900 family groups in the frozen Phase-A internal negative class: bernoulli_fluid, euler_buckling, fourier_heat, gibbs_thomson, helmholtz_resonance, hydrostatics, newtonian_dynamics, torricelli_outflow and young_laplace.
generation: Represent each family by one canonical one-dimensional reduction and use the same 120-point support sampling, 10% local x jitter, eight repeats, nuisance amplitude, 0.5-2.5% response-noise draw and heteroscedastic profile as the curated post-1900 generator.
frozen_evaluation: Reuse the exact Phase-A checkpoint, training memories, calibration-formula empirical CDF, four score components, equal-weight ensemble, top-8 rule and family-median aggregation. Compare all curated future families against the nine generator-matched controls; separately quantify native-internal versus generator-matched-control separability.
random_control: Repeat after the already registered zero-optimization checkpoint and its frozen primary result are available.
interpretation_rule: If generator-matched controls themselves shift upward or the matched-control future AUROC materially collapses, the Phase-A primary separation is generator-confounded. If matched controls remain close to native controls and future AUROC remains high while the random model does not reproduce it, the representation-learning interpretation is strengthened but remains formula-level and post-score diagnostic.
claim_boundary: This diagnostic was motivated by an opened Phase-A result. It cannot be called preregistered, cannot replace a sealed benchmark and supplies no real-measurement discovery rate.
